To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Hubble parameter H 0, the age of the universe t 0, and the critical density ρ c are scale-dependent.
the scale-dependent cosmology provides a viable alternative to the standard Λ CDM model and that it can be used to explain the Hubble constant and the age of Universe problems.
the Universe is not homogeneous, and that the cosmological parameters, such as Ω 0 and H 0, are not constant but depend on the scale of observation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a scale-dependent cosmology which can explain the following cosmological observations.

the following questions: What are the effects of inhomogeneities on the observed properties of the Universe? What can be learned from observations about the inhomogeneous distribution of matter in our Universe? What is the relation between the observed Universe and the underlying homogeneous model?

a cosmology that is based on the following assumptions: (i) the Universe is inhomogeneous, (ii) the Universe is isotropic on large scales, (iii) the Einstein equation is modified on small scales and (iv) the Robertson-Walker (RW) metric is modified on large scales.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scale-dependent cosmology, if true, would not be in conflict with the current data, but would require a revision of the standard cosmological model in a number of ways.

the proposed scale-dependent cosmology, which is based upon the inhomogeneity of the Universe, can explain the observed discrepancy between the local value of H 0 and its value inferred from the CMB anisotropy, and the observed discrepancy between Ω 0 inferred from CMB anisotropic and the value inferred from the local Hubble flow, but cannot explain the age discrepancy.
the scale-dependent cosmology proposed here is consistent with the current observations and that it is a viable alternative to the standard cosmology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a homogeneous and isotropic universe is a good approximation for the large scale structure of our universe.
the inhomogeneous universe can be regarded as a perturbation of the FRW model.
the Universe is inhomogeneous and the scale-dependence of the cosmological parameters is a natural consequence of this inhomogeneity.

the cosmological model proposed here can be tested observationally.
the inhomogeneous universe is a scale-dependent universe.
